answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly: if k bonded identities commit correlated violations, the protocol aggregates their evidence and scales slashing quadratically, O(k²), rather than treating each as an isolated fault. Detection also triggers asymmetric collateral depreciation, so losses compound across the swarm and impose an exponential multiplier on capital destroyed. Splitting stake among velvet, kernel, or pearl identities therefore cannot dilute accountability.
